model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis, logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴) and accuracy in percent (y-axis, linear scale from 35% to 65%) for six different methods: Base (black circles, solid line), FT (blue downward triangles, solid line), IKE (red upward triangles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), MEMIT (purple circles, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). As the co-occurrence number increases, all methods show an upward trend in accuracy, though at different rates. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting near 51% at low co-occurrence and rising to approximately 66% at 10⁴. MEND and MEMIT follow closely, both reaching around 56% at the highest co-occurrence. IKE and FT show moderate gains, ending near 49% and 48% respectively. The Base method exhibits the smallest improvement, plateauing around 44% despite increasing co-occurrence.
